newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -UK traders get defensive as shares fall.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -UK traders get defensive as shares fall.

text.p: The shake out in UK shares on Thursday persuaded options traders to take defensive action as in general they bought puts and sold calls, dealers said.
Ons such deal was in supermarket group Safeway where 500 April 360 puts were bought at 11p.
More aggressive -- because it was out-of-the-money -- was the main deal in Standard Chartered Bank in which 800 April 700 puts were bought at 2p.
Dealers said this may have been as an insurance against the share price falling substantially which would create losses on a shareholding.
By 1340 GMT, Safeway shares were down 1-1/2p to 361p and those of Standard Chartered were 9-1/2p off at 848-1/2p.
Over in railway networks manager Railtrack a belief the shares will not go above 550p by June may have been the reason why 500 June 550 calls were sold at 12p.

If the shares in partly-paid form stay below 550p by June expiry the options seller will make a maximum 12p profit from the deal. The partly paid share lost 2p to 469-1/2p and the second installment of 190p per share is due on June 3.
In oil explorer Lasmo a split synthetic long position was bought.

This involved buying 400 August 260 calls at 16p and selling 400 August 240 puts at 13p -- effectively buying the calls for 3p so that for a profit at expiry the shares need to be above 263p. Lasmo shares added 7p to 243-1/2p.
In FTSE index options, the main deal was from a buyer of 2,000 March 4450 calls at 7p and in European style FTSE there was a seller of 3,500 June 4775 calls at 10-1/2p.
The FTSE 100 index was down 18.9 at 4403.6 by 1340 GMT.
